## My Thinking

I have been farming this same land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My back is not what it used to be, and my two sons both work in Shijiazhuang now. They send money when they can, but the land is still mine to work. I have about 10 mu — I rented out 2 mu to a neighbor's son last year because it is too far from the well, so I am working 8 mu myself this season.

I will grow what I have always grown: winter wheat and then summer maize on the same land. That is what everyone here does. The wheat goes in the ground in October, I harvest it in June, and the maize goes in right after. Two crops from the same field every year. I know this system. My father taught me it, and his father before him.

For seeds, I buy from the village supply shop. The man there sells me the improved wheat seed that the county recommends — I do not save my own wheat seed anymore, the bought seed is better. For maize I always use hybrid seed, the Zhengdan 958 kind. My neighbor has used it for years and gets good yields.

Fertilizer — I use the compound fertilizer bags at planting and then spread urea on the wheat in spring when it starts to green up. I probably put on a bit more than I need, but I would rather the crop not go hungry. For water, the wheat needs three irrigations: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. The maize usually only needs one if the summer rains come as they should. I use the electric pump on my well.

I am too old to plough with the ox. I hire the rotary tiller from the village machinery service after the maize harvest to prepare the wheat seedbed. For the maize I just direct-seed into the wheat stubble — less work and the young men say the soil stays better that way. I spray herbicide and a fungicide on the wheat. Maize I check once and spray if I see army worm.

I do not gamble on new crops I do not understand. At my age, I keep things simple and steady.
